provenance.dataQuality: Weekend US cash market closed. All price and volatility observations are Friday November 20 carried-forward data, not synchronized new Saturday observations. Reuters SOX ~-11%, VIX ~37, 10Y 4.93% approximate and not tick aligned. QQQ -5.67% secondary closing report. VXN and direct CME FedWatch unavailable; no verified contemporaneous 2Y for Reuters 10Y. Prior 4.94%-4.65%=+29 basis points, stale; no valid current curve. Brent 91.53 and WTI 82.47 are stale unmatched-maturity observations, not a reliable current spread. Reuters value-rotation story is context, not proven causal price attribution. Open Watch 174 events, latest Nov 19; no newly curated event.

editorial.marketOverview: Friday November 20 remains the latest US cash session. Reuters reported Nasdaq -5.28%, an approximately 11% semiconductor drop, and VIX near 37; secondary closing data showed QQQ -5.67% against SPY -3.64%. New Reuters reporting describes investors shifting from AI-heavy growth stocks toward value, reinforcing rather than changing the existing risk-off interpretation. No Saturday cash-market price exists.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with the previous 00:38 EST repository assessment, no new curated Open Watch catalyst, synchronized market quote or directional reversal has been established. Additional November 20 Reuters sector-rotation context and an independently published November 23-27 event calendar were reviewed. Outlook unchanged; calendar details refined with Monday 09:45 ET PMI and Tuesday 10:00 ET consumer confidence.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Semiconductor weakness materially exceeded broader market losses, supporting elevated downside risk while also raising short-covering rebound potential. The Friday VIX and breadth readings are approximate and not tick synchronized. The Reuters 10Y 4.93% is not paired with a same-time 2Y; the older 4.94%-4.65%=29bp is correctly scaled but stale. Fed tightening concerns are reported commentary; direct CME probability is not verified. No causal response to an individual Open Watch regulatory event can be isolated.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23 likely opens with elevated downside-continuation and sharp-rebound risk, while 09:45 ET flash PMI could shift rate expectations. Tuesday November 24 tests whether semiconductor leadership stabilizes amid Analog Devices and Dell earnings and consumer-confidence data. Wednesday November 25 concentrates PCE, GDP, durable-goods and jobless-claims releases at 08:30 ET plus the 14:00 ET Beige Book ahead of Thanksgiving. No justified numerical targets without fresh synchronized prices.
editorial.bullCase: A credible rebound needs QQQ and SOX/SMH advancing together, stronger breadth and falling VIX/VXN through Tuesday. Falling Treasury yields and oversold positioning could help, but neither establishes a reversal before cash trading resumes.
editorial.bearCase: Persistently weak semiconductor leadership, elevated volatility and broad selling could extend Friday's decline into Monday and Tuesday. Hawkish PMI/PCE surprises or disappointing AI-hardware earnings could worsen the path, but remain hypothetical future outcomes.
editorial.watchNext: Check Monday opening QQQ, Nasdaq, SOX/SMH, VIX/VXN, breadth and matched 10Y/2Y yields. Refresh direct CME FedWatch and matched Brent/WTI contracts; monitor PMI at 09:45 ET, ADI/Dell earnings Tuesday, Wednesday PCE/GDP and Beige Book, and any genuinely new curated Open Watch event.
